Welcome to South Baddesley Church of England Primary School and Nursery

pageCache.text:
Pupil and
Sports Premium
The following information outlines how South Baddesley spends government-funded ‘Premiums’. This includes Pupil Premium funding, Sports Premium funding and Recovery premium funding (in response to pandemic disruptions to learning).
Pupil Premium Funding
Pupil Premium is funding to improve education outcomes for disadvantaged pupils in schools in England. Evidence shows that disadvantaged children generally face additional challenges in reaching their potential at school and often do not perform as well as other pupils. School leaders can decide on where best to spend their Pupil Premium (and recovery premium) within a framework of approaches set out by the Government.
Children eligible for Pupil Premium funding include those who are registered for free school meals (FSM) or who have been registered for FSM at any point in the last six years (known as ‘Ever 6’), together with children that have been in care continuously for 6 months or more.
PE and Sport Premium Funding
Schools have a central role to play in supporting all children and young people to live healthy active lives. This is particularly true of primary school where the foundations of positive and enjoyable participation in regular physical activity should be established.
Crucial to achieving this is ensuring that pupils have access to at least 30 minutes of physical activity during the school day, alongside high-quality PE provision taught by confident and knowledgeable teachers and opportunities to experience and participate in a wide range of sports and physical activities. PE and sport premium grant funding should be used by schools towards these aims.
Recovery Premium Funding
The recovery premium grant is part of the government’s package of funding to support pupils whose education has been impacted by coronavirus (COVID-19). Over £300m of additional funding for state-funded schools has been allocated in the 2021 to 2022 academic year and £1bn across the 2022 to 2023 and 2023 to 2024 academic years.
It is focused on pupil premium eligible pupils and the most vulnerable pupils who we know have been most impacted. However, schools can use it to deliver evidence-based approaches for supporting any pupil based on an assessment of individual need. As with pupil premium, schools must use their recovery premium on evidence-based approaches to support pupils, guided by a framework of approaches set out by the Government.

pageCache.text:
Wraparound Provision
Summer Holiday Club!
Looking for the perfect way to keep the kids entertained this August?
From 3rd August – 21st August (9am – 3pm Mon - Fri), we are packing every single day with non stop fun!
Farm Activities & Outdoors
Action-Packed Sports & Games
For just £30.00 a day, your child gets a full day of action, plus delicious snacks and lunch refreshments included! Limited places available!
Complete the booking form today (if you are booking for more than one child, please complete a separate form for each child) and we will send over your confirmation. Send your booking form to the Admin Office - adminoffice@southbaddesley.hants.sch.uk
Book your place today!
We are signed up to many childcare voucher schemes including the Government Tax Free Childcare so please do ask in the office and we will be happy to give you all the details you need to start saving money at our wraparound clubs.
We are currently also signed up to Edenred, Sodexo and Computershare but are happy to investigate others if your employer is offering a different scheme.
All parents joining SBS will have a SCOPay account where you can book your Wraparound sessions.
Breakfast Wraparound
Running from 7:45am in the morning, Breakfast Wraparound can give your child a welcoming start to their day at SBS. Children choose a healthy breakfast from a selection of cereals, toast, fruit, yoghurt, juice and water. An array of toys and games are available for the children to play with.
Cost per session: £4
After School Wraparound
Children take part in craft activities and games at our in-house after school wraparound session. A healthy snack is provided and the wraparound session runs till 6pm. There is an option to join at the later time of 4 - 5pm at a reduced rate of £5. This is because children sometimes join us from clubs such as Maths or Nature Club at 4pm.
Cost of 3 - 5pm session: £9
Cost of 5 - 6pm session: £4.50
Some support is available for paying for wraparound care.
Sports After School Clubs
Run by our fantastic, expert Superstar Sports coaches, our sports after school club offers a different session each night including cricket, netball, football, rugby, athletics and performing arts across the year. A healthy snack is provided for sports after school clubs and the clubs run till 5pm.
Cost per session: £9

pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
If you are already familiar with our school, you will know that we often refer to ourselves as SBS. This is not only our name but also our vision. At SBS, we work together so that everyone can S - Strive, B - Believe and S - SHINE.
The Meaning of 'SHINE' at South Baddesley
Our version of SHINE requires different skills to those you may initially think of. It isn't about outperforming others; it is about outgrowing your yesterday.
"To 'shine' at South Baddesley is a personal journey, not a race. We believe that shining means striving to become the very best version of yourself—not in competition with others, but as an inspiration to them. It is about personal growth, integrity, and becoming a role model through your own unique character and kindness."
How we live this every day:
Self-Reflection over Comparison: We celebrate individual milestones and personal bests.
Character as a Skill: We value kindness and integrity as highly as academic achievement.
Leading by Example: Our pupils learn that by being their best selves, they naturally encourage those around them to do the same.
This vision is founded in a culture and ethos of ‘kindness.’ We believe that there are three types of kindness:
kindness to ourselves,
kindness to others and
kindness to the world.
Through our ‘vision and values’ we inspire to develop WISDOM, CURIOSITY, INNOVATION and EXCELLENCE for all our children.
WISDOM - A growth in knowledge, understanding and skills can lead to the ability to show 'wisdom'. Our commitment to 'wisdom' comes from a desire to help children use their new knowledge and skills in a manner that respects humanity, promotes compassion and deep, ethical thinking.
CURIOSITY - The world is an intriguing and amazing place to be and learning helps us to explore our world.
Questions and a thirst to know and do more makes our learning exciting and fun. We believe that curious minds are interested and contented minds. Being curious removes barriers and challenges prejudice.
INNOVATION - Creativity runs deeply through all innovative projects. Combined with a love of problem-solving and deep thinking, innovation can help to build confidence, resourcefulness and opportunities for all learners.
EXCELLENCE - Our ambition is to 'shine' so that we are always achieving the most from our life-long journey in education. Achievements can be demonstrated in many different ways. Excellence doesn't always need to be the loudest contribution to learning but being able to show excellence and to shine, leads to the biggest 'changes' and growth.
As a Church of England Primary School, our vision is rooted in Biblical verse that helps us to understand that to ‘shine.’
'Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven'.

Our School Day
Our school day begins at 8.25am and finishes at 2.55pm.In order to manage traffic on our site, we have a rolling start, 8.25am to 8.35am. This amounts to a total of 32.5 hours for all key stages in a typical week.
Breakfast Club is available for families from 7:45am and a range of after school clubs are available which all run until 5pm. Please see our Wraparound Provision page for details on how to book a space for your child.
